messages:
maria: quick sync — thinking about adding explicit telemetry escape hatches to the onboarding pipeline. premise: when certain telemetry (bench metrics, perf traces) are missing or flaky, we currently block admission. proposal: allow controlled fallback paths with strict guardrails so we don't block useful models while keeping safety
aj: can you sketch the escape paths? are we talking canary-only, reduced SLA, or full admit with warnings? :thinking_face:
sophia: +1 on having multiple graded escape levels. we should differentiate 'no telemetry' vs 'contradictory telemetry' vs 'spiky telemetry'
maria: yep. my notes:
- level 0: block (default)
- level 1: admit to smoke cluster (low qps, isolated namespace) with enhanced sampling for telemetry collection
- level 2: admit to limited production traffic (p95 latency throttled, token budget cap) with automated kill-switch
- level 3: full admit with post-admit audit window
kevin: product concern: how do we surface to customers? we need transparency and opt-in. also legal/regulatory models must remain block-only
aj: technical: need flags at the gate and runtime feature flags. gating logic should be in the coordinator (ingest) not in bench runner. coordinator already knows config and can annotate model metadata
lucas: bench perspective: level 1 -> we need a micro-bench that runs within 10s and reports core signals. current micro-bench takes ~2m for some models. can we craft a minimal probe?
maria: good point. sample probe payload: small prompt set (10 golden prompts), measure: p50/p95 latency, token generation correctness heuristic, OOM detection, kv-cache behavior. if micro-bench > 30s, send level-1 admit to smoke cluster instead
sophia: escape hatch triggers: missing bench result, bench timeout, telemetry ingestion lag > 5m, or recent infra flakiness. we need to store reason codes so we can query why a model was allowed through
aj: config snippet idea for gate policy:
```yaml
admit_policy:
  require_full_telemetry: true
  fallback_policy:
    - reason: bench_timeout
      action: smoke_admit
      max_qps: 5
    - reason: missing_traces
      action: limited_admit
      token_cap_per_min: 1000
```
maria: love that. also add telemetry_ttl and audit_window fields
kevin: UI needs: show current admit level, time since last bench, and a CTA to run immediate micro-bench. also persist historic decisions for compliance
lucas: question: how do we validate quality under limited admits? we shouldn't let hallucinating models reach production. suggest a lightweight semantic-similarity check against golden answers (cosine with threshold) during smoke run
sophia: and if similarity fails, auto-escalate to block and create a high-priority ticket in triage queue. tie into alerting: slack + ticketing
maria: operational controls:
- automatic rollback policy if error rate > X% or latency SLO violated for Y minutes
- manual override for platform on-call
- metric decorators in the model record (why_admitted: bench_timeout, admitted_by: auto-fallback)
aj: implementation notes: coordinator will emit an admit_decision event to eventbus; downstream systems (runtime, console, billing) subscribe and enforce caps. admit_decision schema must be minimal and stable
maria: sample event fields: model_id, admit_level, reason_codes[], timestamp, actor
sophia: we should also XOR this with existing canary policies. escape hatch shouldn't circumvent canary isolation for sensitive tenants
kevin: customers might want to opt-out of any fallback. default should be opt-in for fallback, opt-out flag on tenant config
lucas: bench ops: need a dashboard of all level-1/2 admits so we can prioritize running full bench. maybe auto-schedule full bench within 24h of fallback admit
aj: performance: keeping smoke cluster isolates risk but costs more. consider a quota-based fallback budget per org to control spend
maria: next steps: 1) RFC doc draft with policy enums and event schema 2) coordinator PR with admit_decision emission 3) micro-bench spec (10 prompts + similarity check) 4) console UI mock for admit states
kevin: timeline ask from product: can we have an MVP (only level 1 smoke admit + console flag) in 3 sprints?
maria: realistic. I'll draft RFC this week. @aj can you prototype the admit_event schema? @lucas can you propose the 10 golden prompts?
aj: I'll start schema tomorrow, will post a short PR
lucas: will mock prompts and share samples by EOD Friday
devbot: deploy-bot: reminder — please add feature-flag gating for any runtime changes. :robot_face:
sophia: thanks all. this feels like a good balance between safety and velocity. will comment on RFC once posted
maria: thanks everyone, closing thread unless more asks. :thumbsup:
